summary: Meinrad Scheller (1921–1991) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, and at Paris and Charles University. He held professorships at Fribourg, Munich, and Zurich (1975–1988).
Meiping Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a Tibetologist and historian. He earned a BA at the University of Michigan (~1955–1959) and a PhD at the University of Washington (~1960–1968), then served as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Mengqiu Tian works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned a master's at Heidelberg University (2019–2022) and became an FWO PhD research fellow and doctoral researcher at Ghent University (2025, attested 2026).

Merab Mamardashvili (1930–1990) was a philosopher. He studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1949–1954) and held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Meredith Borthwick (1950–1995) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned degrees from the University of Melbourne (~1968–1972) and the Australian National University (~1973–1980), and headed the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade in 1980.

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980).

Mervyn Sprung (1913–2000) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Manitoba, Toronto, and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD ~1936–1939), and served as Professor of Philosophy at Brock University (1965–1979).
Mery Cecconi is an Indology scholar. She is a PhD candidate at Leiden University under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Mette Halskov Hansen is a scholar of Sinology. She studied at the University of Oslo (MPhil 2020–2022), was a research assistant at Aarhus University (2022–2023), and serves as a professor at the University of Oslo (attested 2026).

Michael Alram is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer at the University of Vienna, later serving as Coin Cabinet Director at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and Austrian Academy of Sciences Vice President.

Michael Aris (1946–1999) was a Tibetologist and historian. He studied at Durham and earned a PhD under David Llewellyn Snellgrove at the University of London, later holding academic posts at Oxford (including St John's, Wolfson, and St Antony's) and Harvard.

Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn (–1988) and served as a Central Asia Specialist at the Royal Library of Berlin from 1988 to 2019.

Michael Baumgarten (1812–1889) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and at Kiel University, where he also held a post (~1839–1846) before serving as Professor of Theology at Rostock (1850–1858).

Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) was an art historian. He studied at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich, and held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, Oxford, the Courtauld Institute of Art, UC Berkeley, and Cornell.

Michael Bernays (1834–1897) studied at the University of Bonn and Heidelberg University, where he studied under Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).
Michael Brunner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He has been abbot at One River Zen (2021) and studied for a Bachelor of Arts at the University of Michigan (2024–2026).
Michael C. Shapiro is an Indologist and linguist. He held an academic career at the University of Washington, serving as Professor (~1970–2017) and later Professor Emeritus of Hindi (~2017).
